subject: biology
title: Synapses Adventure
welcome_lead: Today you'll cross a synapse — neurotransmitter release, receptor binding, and how drugs hijack the process.
meta_desc: A-Level Biology Nervous Coordination — chemical synapses, acetylcholine, exocytosis, summation, and drug action.
final_note: You learned how Ca2+ triggers neurotransmitter exocytosis, how AChR binding depolarises the postsynaptic membrane, and how spatial vs temporal summation work.

concepts.def: Gap between two neurones — signal crosses chemically
Chemical messenger released into synaptic cleft (e.g. acetylcholine)
Postsynaptic ligand-gated channel — opens to Na+ when ACh binds
Enzyme that hydrolyses ACh → acetate + choline (recycled)
Several presynaptic neurones add up to reach threshold
Rapid repeated firing from one neurone adds up to reach threshold

walkthroughs.body_html:
An AP reaches the presynaptic terminal.

1. Voltage-gated Ca²⁺ channels open → Ca²⁺ enters cytoplasm.
2. Vesicles of acetylcholine fuse with presynaptic membrane → exocytosis.
3. ACh diffuses across the cleft.
4. ACh binds AChR on postsynaptic membrane → Na+ channels open → depolarisation.
5. Acetylcholinesterase breaks down ACh; choline reabsorbed.

One signal may not reach threshold. Synapses can add up inputs:

Spatial summation — several presynaptic neurones each release a small amount of neurotransmitter simultaneously onto one postsynaptic cell → combined depolarisation reaches threshold.

Temporal summation — one presynaptic neurone fires many times in quick succession; effects build up before each clears.

Some synapses are inhibitory — open Cl- channels → hyperpolarise, making AP harder.

Drugs can interfere at several points:

- Agonist (e.g. nicotine) — mimics neurotransmitter, binds receptor.
- Antagonist (e.g. curare) — blocks receptor without activating it → paralysis.
- Reuptake inhibitors (e.g. cocaine, SSRIs) — block reabsorption of neurotransmitter → prolonged effect.
- Inhibitors of acetylcholinesterase (e.g. nerve gases) — ACh accumulates → continuous firing.

Synapses ensure one-way transmission and integration of signals.
